from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Signals exist in time and frequency domains.",
            "The Fourier Transform decomposes complex signals.",
            "A guitar pluck illustrates this duality perfectly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Animation elements
        pulse = Dot(color="#FF5733")
        sine = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#33FF57")
        overlap_area = Rectangle(width=1, height=1, color="#FFFF33", fill_opacity=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pulse))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(pulse.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(sine))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fixed: place_in_area returns the mobject, which must be part of an animation
        self.place_in_area(overlap_area, "C2", "D4")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.play(FadeIn(overlap_area))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Duality Challenge", [
            "Signals narrow in time broaden in frequency.",
            "A brief pulse requires infinite frequencies.",
            "This is the core duality challenge."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a point particle (#33A1FF) representing classical focus.
        particle = Dot(color="#33A1FF")
        self.place_at_grid(particle, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(particle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33A1FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Expand the point into a wave packet (#A133FF).
        wave_packet = VGroup(
            *[Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color="#A133FF") for _ in range(10)]
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_packet, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(particle, wave_packet))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#A133FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the trade-off between localization in space and frequency.
        trade_off_viz = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE),
            Dot(color="#33A1FF"),
            Dot(color="#A133FF")
        )
        self.place_in_area(trade_off_viz, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(trade_off_viz))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Formulation (The Bound)", [

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The Gaussian is the optimal signal.", "It acts as a perfect window.", "Engineers use it to balance domains.", "Detecting short chirps requires this precision.", "It provides the ideal processing balance."]
        self.setup_layout("The Optimal Solution: Gabor Atoms", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in the Gaussian function (#FF5733) as the envelope.
        gaussian = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#FF5733")
        self.place_in_area(gaussian, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(gaussian))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Modulate the Gaussian with a sine carrier wave (#33FF57).
        sine_carrier = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2) * np.sin(5 * x), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#33FF57")
        self.place_in_area(sine_carrier, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(gaussian.copy(), sine_carrier))
        self.play(Create(sine_carrier))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Scale the Gaussian width to match the optimal bound.
        self.play(gaussian.animate.stretch(0.5, dim=0), sine_carrier.animate.stretch(0.5, dim=0))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application: Modern Communication", [
            "We cannot localize perfectly in both.",
            "Resolution choice depends on specific goals.",
            "Radar systems exemplify this critical trade-off.",
            "Bats use pulses for different tasks.",
            "Choosing resolution governs modern signal processing."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        spectrum = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 0.5], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        graph = spectrum.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) * np.exp(-0.2*x) + 1, color=WHITE)
        atoms = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color="#33FF33").move_to(spectrum.c2p(i, 1)) for i in range(1, 9, 2)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33A1FF")
        self.place_in_area(spectrum, "B1", "E3")
        self.play(Create(spectrum), Create(graph))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33A1FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33A1FF")
        self.play(FadeIn(atoms))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#33A1FF")
        self.play(atoms.animate.set_color("#33A1FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#33FF33")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Pulse and the Wave
sections.content: Briefly define the two domains: the Time Domain (where a signal lives) and the Frequency Domain (what a signal is made of). Introduce the Fourier Transform as a prism that decomposes a complex signal into its constituent pure frequencies.
sections.example: Visualizing a pluck of a guitar string (time) vs. the distinct musical pitch it produces (frequency).

sections.title: The Duality Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the core conflict: 'How narrow can a signal be in time before it becomes broad in frequency?' Use graphical overlays showing a sharp spike (Dirac delta) spreading out into a flat line (constant frequency spectrum) and vice versa.
sections.example: A 'Blink': A camera shutter opening and closing instantly captures a single moment, but requires an infinite range of frequencies to define that sudden jump.

sections.title: Mathematical Formulation (The Bound)
sections.content: Present the Heisenberg-Gabor Uncertainty Principle: Δt · Δf ≥ 1/(4π). Explain that this is not a measurement error, but a fundamental property of wave motion. Show a plot of the product of standard deviations shrinking to a limit.
sections.example: A Gaussian wave packet: Animation showing that squeezing the bell curve in the time graph automatically forces it to widen in the frequency graph.

sections.title: The Optimal Solution: Gabor Atoms
sections.content: Introduce the 'perfect' balance. Explain that the Gaussian function is the unique signal that minimizes this uncertainty product, acting as the ideal 'window' for signal processing.
sections.example: A sound engineer trying to detect a short chirp: Using a Gaussian window to balance the need to know 'when' the sound happened and 'what' note it played.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Modern Communication
sections.content: Summarize how this trade-off governs reality. Conclude that we cannot perfectly localize a signal in time and frequency simultaneously; we must choose the resolution that fits our specific goal.
sections.example: Radar systems: A bat (the biological sonar expert) uses short, broad-frequency pulses to locate mosquitoes (timing) vs. long, constant-frequency pulses to track speed (Doppler).
